name: Cardarine + SR9009 endurance stack

card.summary: A pairing of two research compounds, GW501516 and SR9009, used by some lifters to chase endurance and leanness, which they link to a lighter, more defined physique.
card.note: Neither compound is approved for human use; GW501516 is banned by WADA and linked to cancer in animals.

quick.overview:
The stack combines cardarine (GW501516, a PPAR-delta agonist) with SR9009 (Stenabolic, a Rev-erb agonist). Both are sold online as research chemicals alongside SARMs and are discussed for endurance, fat loss and leanness.

The appearance chain users describe is more cardio capacity, more training and a leaner, more defined body. The compounds have mouse and rat research behind them and no approved use; a human study of GW501516 compared it with placebo, and clinical safety data are limited.
quick.how: Users take them orally as capsules or liquids alongside training and cardio and often stack them with SARMs. Specific amounts, cycles and sources are not covered here. Cardarine is also discussed as a cut aid and as an alternative to clenbuterol.
quick.risks: GSK stopped development of GW501516 in 2007, and animal studies later showed rapid cancers in several organs; WADA banned it in 2009 and warned that approval will not be given. SR9009 is also on WADA's prohibited list and lacks human safety data. Case reports describe hormone disruption and liver injury with products sold as SARMs, which often contain other undeclared compounds.

lead: The cardarine and SR9009 stack pairs GW501516, a PPAR-delta agonist, with SR9009, a Rev-erb agonist. Both are "non-SARM" research compounds sold in the same markets as SARMs, and users talk about them as endurance and fat-loss aids.[7][8]

GW501516 was developed by Ligand Pharmaceuticals and GlaxoSmithKline starting in 1992; GSK discontinued development in 2007 and later animal work showed rapid cancers in several organs. In 2007 Ronald Evans's lab reported major endurance gains in mice.[7] WADA banned it in 2009 and says clinical approval will not be given.[7]

SR9009, associated with Thomas Burris of Scripps Research, increased exercise capacity and muscle mitochondria in mice, and is on WADA's list as a hormone and metabolic modulator. The wiki page records no human clinical data.[8]
Forum users discuss both for leanness; analytic and case-report literature documents mislabelled products and harms.[1][3][5]

chain: Higher endurance and fat-burning capacity (claimed, from animal work)
angle.text: Users take the stack to support endurance and leanness, expecting longer cardio and a more defined physique. The support comes largely from animal studies.

paras: GW501516 is a highly selective PPAR-delta agonist that recruits PGC-1alpha and raises genes for energy expenditure; in rats it boosted fat breakdown in muscle, and in obese monkeys it raised HDL.[7] SR9009 strengthens repression by Rev-erb; in mice it raised exercise capacity and muscle mitochondria.[8]

On looksmax.org, teenagers and others ask about cardarine for leanmaxxing, and replies suggest alternatives and joke about cancer.[9][10] Threads compare it with clenbuterol and discuss running it with HGH.[11] T Nation posters list cardarine among many compounds ordered at once, while others note it is not a SARM but a PPAR agonist and raise mutagenicity concerns.[12][13]

GSK halted GW501516 and animal studies reported rapid cancers; a 2018 mouse study linked it to faster colitis-associated colorectal cancer.[7] A case report described gynecomastia and hypogonadism in a man using supplements found to contain RAD-140, MK-677 and cardarine.[1] A case involving GW1516 with ostarine and a review of liver injury tied to performance-enhancing products advertised on social media are also reported.[2][3] Market studies in Europe found SARMs, metabolic modulators and secretagogues in suspected illegal medicines.[4]
No clinical studies of the combined stack were found. A 2021 human study compared GW501516 with placebo, and SR9009 data are from cells and animals.[7][8]

timeline.event: Ligand and GSK begin the collaboration that produced GW501516.[7]
GSK stops development; Evans lab reports mouse endurance gains.[7]

lore.intro: Cardarine is a common leanmaxxing topic on looksmax.org and T Nation.[9][11][12]

claims.believers: Users ask about it for fat loss and one thread title says anyone leanmaxxing without it is not trying.[9]
claims.experts: Animal studies show fat-burning effects, but development was halted over cancer findings and WADA warned of health risks.[7]

claims.claim: Cardarine is not a SARM and is safe to defend
claims.believers: A T Nation poster says it belongs to PPAR agonists rather than SARMs.[12]
claims.experts: Other posters cite mutagenic concerns, matching animal cancer findings.[7][13]
